exercises.translation: I will buy something, without specifying what. Formation: complete the phrase. Use the 何か/何も family, alone or with the ordinary subject/object case marker where suitable; do not add a contrastive は.
exercises.evidence: The required reference and case role are explicit; the whole predicate fixes the negative scope where requested.
exercises.explanation: The unspecified か expression does not identify which referent; the も expression combines with the negative predicate to exclude all relevant referents from this action/state. A negative predicate alone is not a rule to replace every か with も. 何か can retain を for the object or が for the subject; in this ordinary negative pattern, 何も replaces that subject/object marking. Kana and fitting casual variants are accepted.

options.rationale: Leaves a referent unspecified rather than expressing the no-member pattern.

options.label: 何も
options.rationale: In the taught negative pattern, excludes every relevant referent; it does not mean some unspecified one.

exercises.translation: I will ask someone, without specifying whom. Formation: complete the phrase. Form the whole indefinite/negative phrase and retain the case marker: に for the person asked, と for the conversation partner.
exercises.evidence: The required reference and case role are explicit; the whole predicate fixes the negative scope where requested.
exercises.explanation: The unspecified か expression does not identify which referent; the も expression combines with the negative predicate to exclude all relevant referents from this action/state. A negative predicate alone is not a rule to replace every か with も. Keep the person's role: 誰かに/誰にも for the person asked, and 誰かと/誰とも for the conversation partner. か comes before the retained case particle; も follows it. The corresponding どなた forms are more respectful and are also accepted, including their recognized 何方 spelling; kana remains the ordinary model.
